--- title: "Speech perception: identification" subtitle: "Automatically generated task sheet · L_ORAL_FON_PC_IDENTIFICA" --- ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} **Automatically generated task sheet** (A · Accuracy; quality class C). Generated on November 28, 2026 with `scripts/R/ficha_generica_v3.R --tarea L_ORAL_FON_PC_IDENTIFICA`. Figures come from the data; the theoretical framework is shared by the tasks of the same construct. **Interpretation and team review are missing.** Spanish name: *Percepción del habla: identificación*. [Spanish version](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/auto/L_ORAL_FON_PC_IDENTIFICA.html). ::: ::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"} **Class C.** It was given to few children, at few time points or in different versions. The task sheet documents the task and its first data; figures are descriptive and cannot yet be used as norms. [What each class means](../../limites.en.qmd#sec-clases). ::: **In one sentence.** Speech perception: identification, from age 4 to 6 (2,524 administrations in 4 cohorts). AUC .51–.61 against persistent reading difficulty. ## Description | | | |---|---| | Codes | 2007 | | Battery | SERNICLAES | | Format | auditory stimuli | | Items | — | | Task family | A · Accuracy | | Score | Correct responses | | Instructions (platform) | INSTRUCCIONES Tenemos un amigo extraterrestre que está aprendiendo a hablar nuestro idioma. Al pobre le está costando muchísimo y sólo puede decir la primera sílaba (trocito) de cada palabra. *(Spanish)* | ## Theoretical framework The **categorical perception** tasks (Serniclaes battery) use synthetic syllables ranging from BA to PA in voicing steps. In identification, the child says which syllable they hear; in discrimination, whether two syllables are the same or different. **Minimal pairs** ask the child to decide whether two real syllables are the same or different. They measure the precision of phonemic categories, the basis of letter–sound correspondences. **Phonological fluency** (saying, in 30 seconds, words that begin with a given phoneme) measures something else: lexical access from a sound and executive control. **What the evidence says:** - **Dyslexia shows a categorical perception deficit, clearer in discrimination.** A meta-analysis confirms the deficit compared with children of the same age and with younger readers at the same level. The effect is larger in discrimination than in identification [@noordenbos2015meta]. - **In Spanish, what fails is the boundary between categories.** In 204 Spanish children, those with dyslexia discriminated pairs that cross the phonemic boundary worse and some within-category differences better (allophonic perception) [@serniclaes2021allophonic]. That is why the total of correct responses mixes two effects of opposite sign. - **Its predictive value is modest and not entirely phonological.** In 237 children, perception at age 5½ predicted reading a year later without going through phonemic awareness. These tasks also capture decision making [@snowling2019speech]. In another study, its effect on decoding disappeared when phonological processing was controlled [@mcbridechang1997growth]. The evidence is therefore contradictory. - **Phonological fluency reflects access, not representations.** In 66 Greek children with dyslexia or developmental language disorder, word production was lower, but the size of clusters of related words was the same as in 83 controls [@mengisidou2019fluency]. **What our data show.** - **Categorical perception.** Discrimination does not predict persistent difficulty (AUC .39–.53) and identification barely does (.51–.63). This is to be expected if the total of correct responses is scored: the identification slope and between- and within-category discrimination should be computed from the item-by-item responses. - **Minimal pairs.** Low stability (ρ = .07–.39) and AUC from .45 to .69, better from age 5. Against Woodcock-Muñoz, .63–.66 at ages 6–7. - **Phonological fluency.** A single session at age 5 (793 children, almost all from Preleo schools): AUC of .68 against persistent difficulty and of .59–.62 against low comprehension. It is related to phonological awareness, letters and reading (ρ = .41–.43). ## Sample and descriptive statistics | Time point| Cohort| Session|School year | N| Non-Preleo| Preleo| Schools| |----------:|------:|-------:|:-----------|---:|----------:|------:|-------:| | 4.3| 2012| 158|2016/17 | 384| 380| 0| 17| | 5.2| 2011| 156|2016/17 | 895| 0| 895| 35| | 5.2| 2014| 907|2019/20 | 331| 13| 318| 20| | 6.2| 2010| 155|2016/17 | 914| 264| 650| 34| | Time point| N| Cohorts| Mean| SD| Median| Skewness| % floor| % ceiling| |----------:|---:|-------:|-----:|----:|------:|--------:|-------:|---------:| | 4.3| 380| 2012| 11.87| 5.24| 11| -0.18| 5.53| 14.74| | 6.2| 264| 2010| 12.17| 4.34| 11| -0.13| 2.65| 9.85| **Score range** (non-Preleo group, in correct responses). The usual range goes from P1 to P99 (98% of the children). The minimum–maximum is the one observed after cleaning. | Time point| N|Usual range (P1–P99) |Min.–max. | Warning| |----------:|---:|:--------------------|:---------|-------:| | 4.3| 380|0–20 |0–20 | | | 6.2| 264|0–20 |0–20 | | ## Reliability There are no two time points with the same children (at least 80). ## Validity **Concurrent.** Outside its domain, the highest relation is with: Rapid naming (RAN) (4.3, r = .13); Rapid naming (RAN) (5.2, r = .10); Word and text reading (6.2, r = .03). **Against reading difficulty and comprehension.** Against persistent difficulty, AUC .51–.61. Against poor comprehension one or two school years later (non-circular criterion), AUC .45–.55. ![Validity: AUC with 95% confidence interval (labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_L_ORAL_FON_PC_IDENTIFICA_F2_validez.png){width=85%} **Against an external criterion, years later.** Against low Woodcock-Muñoz reading fluency in 2021/22 ([chapter](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/criterio-woodcock.html), *in Spanish*), AUC .47–.62 (2 time points; 266–270 children). ## Provisional norms | Time point| N| Cohorts| P5| P10| P16| P25| P50| P75| P90| |----------:|-----:|----------:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 4.3| 380| 2012| 0.0| 6| 8| 9| 11| 15| 20| | 5.2| 1,226| 2011, 2014| 0.0| 5| 9| 10| 11| 14| 19| | 6.2| 264| 2010| 5.2| 8| 10| 10| 11| 15| 19| These are norms by time point (school year × term). For dates between assessments and time points without a normative sample, study M3 proposes continuous norms on **months of instruction**, not on age, with relative age within the school year as an adjustment. ![Provisional norms (non-Preleo schools; labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_L_ORAL_FON_PC_IDENTIFICA_F1_baremo.png){width=85%} ## Variables that affect it |Variable | Time point| n| Effect| p| |:---------------------------------------|----------:|-----:|------:|-----:| |School SES (ρ) | 4.3| 268| -0.073| 0.235| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 4.3| 384| 0.166| 0.104| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 4.3| 380| 0.090| 0.078| |School (ICC) | 4.3| 384| 0.112| | |School SES (ρ) | 5.2| 1,224| 0.003| 0.907| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 5.2| 1,186| 0.023| 0.694| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 5.2| 1,206| -0.012| 0.678| |School (ICC) | 5.2| 1,226| 0.090| | |School SES (ρ) | 6.2| 914| -0.050| 0.131| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 6.2| 912| -0.119| 0.076| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 6.2| 911| 0.027| 0.411| |School (ICC) | 6.2| 914| 0.042| | ## For publications The LEEDUCA platform task “Speech perception: identification” (code 2007; SERNICLAES battery) assesses speech perception. Stimuli are presented auditorily and the child responds by selecting on the screen. The time limit is 180 seconds. It is administered individually on a computer at school. In the 2010, 2011, 2012 and 2014 cohorts it was administered in 4 sessions, from 4 to 6 years of age. The main outcome is the number of correct responses. Against later poor reading comprehension, AUC = .45–.55. ## Pending issues - Write the interpretation; review with the team.
